title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Pittsburgh, PA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Pittsburgh steel, bridge and shale-gas welders: D1.1, D1.5 or API 1104 for Part C, Part B planning. Online or on site.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Pittsburgh: Six Days for Steel, Bridge and Pipeline Welding Inspectors
html:
Pittsburgh's welding work is heavy, old and outdoors. Coke batteries and blast furnaces in the Monongahela Valley need constant repair. Hundreds of steel bridges cross three rivers and countless ravines. Gas from the Marcellus and Utica shales moves through gathering lines and compressor stations across the hills of Washington, Greene, Butler and Beaver counties. All of it produces welds that someone must measure, judge against a code and sign for, and in western Pennsylvania that someone is often expected to hold the American Welding Society's Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) credential.

Atlantis NDT offers a six-day exam-preparation course for that credential, aimed at welders, fitters, quality control inspectors, NDT technicians and engineers around Pittsburgh. AWS sets the CWI exam, marks it and grants the certification; Atlantis has no hand in any of those steps and AWS has neither approved nor endorsed the course. Candidates qualify with AWS on their own education, experience and eyesight. Someone preparing alone gets online access with a study plan, materials, original practice items and an instructor who answers questions by message. A mill contractor, fabricator or pipeline company can instead host the six days at its own site for a group of employees. The national CWI exam prep page carries the full outline; what follows is the Pittsburgh view.

Mon Valley steelmaking and the repair work it never stops producing

U.S. Steel's Mon Valley Works, which includes the Edgar Thomson plant in Braddock and the Clairton coke works, is the region's best-known steel operation, and U.S. Steel has been owned by Nippon Steel since mid-2025. Integrated steelmaking is hard on equipment. Ladles, hoods, ductwork, conveyor structures, crane runways and coke oven hardware crack, wear and distort under heat and load, and much of that damage is fixed by welding during short outages.

That kind of maintenance teaches a candidate things the exam rewards. Repair welders learn quickly why preheat matters on thick sections, why a crack has to be removed to sound metal before it is rewelded, and how hydrogen and restraint combine to crack a weld hours after it was made. They also meet unusual steels: abrasion-resistant plate, castings, and older grades of unknown chemistry. Those are exactly the metallurgy and discontinuity topics in Part A.

Mill and contractor QC staff tend to be weaker on paperwork. Repair procedures in a mill are often informal, and code book navigation is a skill many experienced maintenance people never needed. The six days spend real time on reading welding procedure documents and on finding the right clause fast. Atlantis also supports steel producers directly through steel industry NDT consulting in Pittsburgh, and the techniques used on mill structures are covered in magnetic particle inspection of structural steel and ultrasonic testing for steel mills.

Bridges, and the lesson of Fern Hollow

Pittsburgh is famous for its bridges, and it learned in January 2022 how much depends on inspecting them. The Fern Hollow Bridge, a steel frame bridge carrying Forbes Avenue over Frick Park, fell on the morning of January 28, 2022. Federal investigators later linked the collapse to heavy corrosion and loss of section in the steel legs, conditions that earlier inspections had noted but that were never repaired. A replacement bridge opened before the end of that year.

Fern Hollow was a corrosion and maintenance failure rather than a welding failure, but its effect on the region's work is clear. Bridge owners in Allegheny County and across PennDOT's western districts now run large programs of steel repair, member replacement and full superstructure renewal. Fabricating and repairing that steel brings in AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, with its stricter rules for fracture-critical members, its controls on filler metal and heat input, and its demand for documented inspection at each stage.

For a CWI candidate the bridge market offers two kinds of jobs. Shop QC inspectors at bridge fabricators check fit-up, preheat, weld size and finished profile before the owner's representative arrives. Field inspectors working for consultants or the owner verify repairs, bolted and welded splices, and new members during erection. Both need confident symbol reading and a firm grip on visual acceptance criteria. AWS offers a D1.5 endorsement once you hold the CWI, and the D1.5 overview is a good place to see how it differs from the structural code.

Shale gas: pipe, stations and a cracker plant down the river

Since the late 2000s, natural gas drilling has reshaped the counties around Pittsburgh. Each well pad feeds gathering lines that lead to compressor stations, processing plants and larger transmission pipelines. Building that network means a great deal of pipe welding to API 1104, and the transmission and station piping falls under federal pipeline safety rules in 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, which reference API 1104 for welder and procedure qualification and for acceptance.

Downriver in Beaver County, the Shell polyethylene plant at Monaca, built to turn ethane from the shale fields into plastic pellets, began operating in 2022. A plant of that size involves miles of process piping, pressure vessels and storage tanks, all welded to procedures qualified under ASME Section IX, with the piping governed by B31.3 and topped up by the operator's company standards. Turnarounds and expansions at plants like it keep contract welders and inspectors busy across the Ohio River valley.

Pipeline construction inspectors who carry a CWI are common on Appalachian spreads. If you work there, the API 1104 overview explains the standard you are most likely to bring to Part C, and Atlantis sends technicians for pipeline inspection in the Pittsburgh area.

Who signs off welds in western Pennsylvania

Pittsburgh CWI openings come from a recognizable set of employers, and each judges a candidate a little differently.

Employer typeTypical code baseWhat they look for
Steel producers and mill maintenance contractorsOwner specifications, AWS D1.1 for structuresRepair experience, preheat discipline, metallurgy, quick judgment during outages
Bridge and structural fabricatorsAWS D1.5, AWS D1.1Shop QC records, fit-up checks, symbol fluency, fracture-critical awareness
Engineering and inspection consultants for PennDOT and countiesAWS D1.5, state specificationsField verification of repairs and new steel, clear daily reports
Pipeline and midstream contractorsAPI 1104, 49 CFR 192 and 195Welder qualification checks, visual acceptance on the spread, documentation
Petrochemical and power maintenance contractorsASME Section IX, B31.1, B31.3Procedure compliance, heat treatment records, turnaround pace
Testing and special inspection agenciesAWS D1.1 under the Pennsylvania UCCThird-party verification on building steel for owners and code officials

Inspection firms that combine visual welding inspection with ultrasonic, magnetic particle or penetrant methods are another large employer. Atlantis performs weld inspection in Pittsburgh at customer sites, and it is a good example of work where the CWI and employer-certified NDT qualifications sit side by side.

The Pittsburgh Section of AWS

AWS groups its members into numbered districts, each made up of local sections. Pittsburgh has its own section in District 7. Section meetings and tours are useful while you study, because the people in the room include mill metallurgists, bridge shop QC managers, pipeline inspectors and welding instructors, many of whom took the CWI exam themselves. Ask them which code book their employer prefers and how long they spent on Part B preparation. Officers and meeting venues change, so check the District 7 listing on aws.org for current contacts.

Where Pittsburgh welders learn the trade

The Community College of Allegheny County (CCAC) offers a welding technology certificate, and it is one common starting point for welders in the city. Union apprenticeship programs for boilermakers, ironworkers and pipefitters train many of the people who later move into inspection, as do private welding schools across the region. Graduates of any of these routes arrive with good hand skills and some code exposure, but they still need years of welding-related work before AWS will let them sit the CWI exam.

For those graduates, the CWI is a medium-term goal rather than a next step. Starting early helps: keep records of every job, the codes you worked to, and a supervisor who can confirm your duties. Those records become your experience evidence when you apply.

Booking the three exam parts from Pittsburgh

AWS delivers the CWI exam in two ways. The Fundamentals paper (Part A, 150 questions) and the open-book Code Application paper (Part C, between about 50 and 65 questions) are on-screen tests at Prometric sites, and AWS counts more than 100 of those in the US. Once AWS sends your confirmation letter, its eligibility code lets you book them, usually close to home.

The Practical (Part B) involves hands-on tasks with tools and specimens AWS provides, plus 46 questions, and it is held only at AWS seminar locations on fixed dates. Pittsburgh candidates should look up the nearest location and its schedule on aws.org first, because that date anchors the rest of the plan. AWS requires 72% or better on each of the three parts. AWS publishes its exam and seminar fees on aws.org; a budgeting guide for the CWI exam helps you add travel and books. To see which part trips candidates most, read the part-by-part analysis.

Which code book to carry into Part C

AWS lets each candidate pick one code for the open-book part. Its accepted list covers AWS D1.1, D1.2, D1.5, D15.1 and D17.1, API 1104, an ASME Section IX option paired with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option, each tied to an edition named on aws.org. For Pittsburgh, the usual pattern looks like this:

  • Mill, structural and special inspection work: AWS D1.1. It is also the best base if you want to add D1.5 later.
  • Bridge fabrication and repair: AWS D1.5 directly, or D1.1 followed by the D1.5 endorsement.
  • Gas gathering and transmission: API 1104.
  • Petrochemical and power plant maintenance: the ASME option.

Background reading before Day 4: the structural code summary, the Section IX qualification overview and the guide to procedure and welder qualification records. Writing and qualifying procedures is outside the services Atlantis offers, yet the exam expects you to check a job against one.

How the six days map onto Pittsburgh work

DayCourse blockWhere Pittsburgh candidates usually focus
1Fundamentals I: processes, joints, AWS A3.0 terms, AWS A2.4 symbolsMill welders know stick and flux cored well but often need drilling on symbols with supplementary marks.
2Fundamentals II: metallurgy, testing, flaw formation, NDT, safety, inspector conductPreheat on thick and unknown steels, hydrogen cracking, and what Charpy toughness means for bridge members.
3Practical: gauges, weld size and contour, acceptance against supplied documentsOn-site groups use their own fillet and bridge cam gauges and real shop samples; Atlantis does not ship replica kits.
4Code application in the chosen bookFinding tables fast, especially preheat tables and visual acceptance criteria.
5Timed practice papers for all three partsPacing on the 150-question Fundamentals paper and on code lookups.
6Targeted review, exam-day planning, application checklistPulling scattered job records into a clean experience history.

The practice items are Atlantis's own, drafted from the topic outline AWS publishes; no real exam question appears in them. The course describes what is taught, not what score anyone will get.

Experience rules for steelworkers, pipeliners and maintenance welders

AWS scales the required years of welding-related work to your schooling; the national page carries the whole table. A western Pennsylvania welder with a high school diploma needs five years. A CCAC certificate or similar completed trade training usually falls in the vocational row, which lowers that to four, though AWS has the final say. A two-year degree in engineering technology, engineering or physical science lowers it to two. Shorter formal schooling raises the requirement to nine or twelve years.

Steelworkers often have long service but mixed duties; AWS counts only work it accepts as welding-related, so describe your welding tasks plainly. Pipeline welders who travel from spread to spread should keep a running log, since contractors change and memories fade. Eyesight is assessed separately: AWS needs a visual acuity record on its own form, completed within the period it allows before the exam.

Beyond the CWI: endorsements and NDT certification

Once certified, a CWI follows a nine-year cycle that AWS sets out on aws.org, with renewals in years three and six and a recertification route at year nine. Pittsburgh inspectors often add endorsements for D1.5 bridge work, API 1104 pipelines or the magnetic particle and penetrant methods, and some go on to the Senior CWI step.

Others move toward nondestructive testing. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employing company certifies its NDT staff to its written practice; Atlantis provides training on that basis, such as VT Level 2, and lists local options under NDT training in Pittsburgh. For a straight comparison of credentials, see CWI against API 577 and ASNT Level II. To rehearse weld inspection steps between study sessions, try the Practical NDT welding workshop.

Neighboring markets have their own pages: CWI exam prep in Cleveland, Cincinnati and Philadelphia.

Tell Atlantis how many people are preparing, the code book each one plans to use, and whether they will study online or need the six days at your mill, shop or yard (with its address). Send it through the Pittsburgh CWI exam prep quote request, and expect a reply within one business day.

faq.q: Should a Pittsburgh bridge inspector choose D1.5 or D1.1 for Part C?
faq.a: Either works. Highway bridge steel is welded to D1.5, so that book suits people already working in bridge shops. D1.1 is broader and makes a solid base, and AWS offers a D1.5 endorsement you can add after certification.

faq.q: I weld at a steel mill. Does mill repair work count as experience?
faq.a: Welding-related work on production, repair or maintenance can count, but AWS makes the final decision. Describe your welding duties clearly and have a supervisor ready to confirm them.

faq.q: What code book suits shale gas pipeline work?
faq.a: API 1104 is the standard most gathering and transmission contractors work to, and federal pipeline rules reference it. It is one of the books AWS accepts for Part C.

faq.q: Where do Pittsburgh candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are on-screen tests at Prometric sites, booked with your AWS eligibility code. Part B happens only at AWS seminar locations on set dates, so look up the nearest one on aws.org.

faq.q: Is the course taught in a Pittsburgh classroom?
faq.a: No. Solo candidates study online with an instructor answering their questions, while a company can bring the course onto its own mill floor, shop or yard for six days. Atlantis has two offices, in Houston and Hyderabad; everywhere else the work happens at the customer site or online.

faq.q: Does finishing the course make me a CWI?
faq.a: No. AWS sets the exam, marks it and grants the certificate. Atlantis provides preparation, has no view of exam content and carries no AWS approval or endorsement.

faq.q: Do I need to know NDT for the exam?
faq.a: You need to know what each common NDT method can and cannot find, which Fundamentals covers. Performing NDT is a separate qualification, certified by the employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A for most US companies.

faq.q: Are the practice questions real exam questions?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes them from the AWS topic outline. Nothing on the practice papers is taken from an actual AWS examination.

faq.q: How long does the CWI stay valid?
faq.a: AWS describes a nine-year life for the certificate, with renewal paperwork at year three and year six and a recertification step when the nine years run out. Details are on the national course page and aws.org.

faq.q: How do I request a quote?
faq.a: Use the Pittsburgh quote request with your headcount, code books and site address. Atlantis replies within one business day.
